summary: This article explains how desert locusts change from shy loners into huge hungry swarms after rain, how they grow, how far they fly, and how countries work together to stop them.
introduce: Show the title “Locusts: Swarms Across Deserts” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: to shed an old skin, shell, or feathers so new ones can grow
a huge, spinning storm that forms over warm seas and brings strong wind and rain

challengeTerms.def: liking to live or be in groups
plants in general, especially those growing in an area
a sudden start or rise of something harmful, such as pests or a disease

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a tiny insect can be a bigger danger to farms than a large animal? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why heavy rain in the desert can lead to problems for farmers far away.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review solitary, molt, and cyclone, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use gregarious, vegetation, and outbreak in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
